title: Federal Programs Liaison Note: Records Lead for UCFE and UCX Appeals (Unemployment Insurance Appeals)
content:
Under Unemployment Insurance Appeals, when an appeal's first hearing is set, the program of the appealed claim is read from the claim itself — the program its Unemployment Benefit Claims record is filed under.

**Rule.** The first-setting federal records lead is the federal-employee records days when the appealed claim is an Unemployment Compensation for Federal Employees (UCFE) claim, the ex-servicemember records days when it is an Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Servicemembers (UCX) claim, and zero days when it is a claim under any other program or the appeal names no claim. The first hearing date found from the first-setting clock and the first-setting target is moved later by this lead before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied.

| Program of the appealed claim | First-setting federal records lead |
|---|---|
| Unemployment Compensation for Federal Employees (UCFE) | 10 calendar days |
| Unemployment Compensation for Ex-Servicemembers (UCX) | 7 calendar days |
| any other program | 0 days |
| the appeal names no claim (for example an employer's contribution rate appeal) | 0 days |

## Points of judgement

- The claim read is the one the appeal names. Other claims the claimant may hold, under other programs, do not decide the lead.
- The lead is in calendar days and moves the first hearing date found from the clock and the target later, ahead of the notice minimum and the weekend rule.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* a claimant appeals a separation determination on a UCX claim. The first hearing date found from the clock and the target, Tuesday 5 May 2026, moves 7 days later to Tuesday 12 May before the notice minimum and the weekend rule are applied. Had the claim been a UCFE claim, it would move 10 days, to Friday 15 May.
